title: Taswira · The earth becomes a city

clips.disputed: Who finished Kano's first wall? The Kano Chronicle credits Yusa (1136–1194 by its reckoning); Nigeria's 2007 UNESCO tentative-list file credits Zamnagawa, in the mid-14th century. The age of the Dala settlement also differs: the 7th century (Iliffe) or the 10th (UNESCO file).

features.name: Kano · walled city
features.location: Representative point for the old walled city, rounded; not a survey of the walls or gates.

features.name: Katsina
features.location: Today's city centre, rounded. The fifteenth-century town's extent is not drawn.

natural-earth.title: Natural Earth: 1:10m and 1:50m land, 1:10m lakes, 1:10m rivers and lake centrelines
natural-earth.author: Natural Earth (Nathaniel Vaughn Kelso, Tom Patterson and contributors)
natural-earth.rights: Public domain (Natural Earth terms of use). Cut and simplified for this page.
natural-earth.checked: Terms of use opened 27 Oct 2026. Reservoirs (such as Kainji, 1968) are left out because they did not exist before 1914; see history/geo/README.md.

kano-chronicle-wiki.title: Kano Chronicle
kano-chronicle-wiki.author: Wikipedia contributors (describes and links H. R. Palmer, "The Kano Chronicle", Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 38, 1908, pp. 58-98)
kano-chronicle-wiki.kind: encyclopedia overview of a primary source; used only to describe the Chronicle and Palmer's translation
kano-chronicle-wiki.rights: Facts cited; no text reproduced beyond short names.
kano-chronicle-wiki.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. The Chronicle is a compilation of oral tradition and older documents; the copy Palmer translated (1908) was written down in the late nineteenth century. It gives reigns by length, so calendar years are reckoned by later editors.

last-1980-kano-chronicle.title: Historical Metaphors in the Kano Chronicle
last-1980-kano-chronicle.author: Murray Last, History in Africa 7 (1980), pp. 161-178
last-1980-kano-chronicle.kind: peer-reviewed historiography (first page and abstract read; full text paywalled)
last-1980-kano-chronicle.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026 (first page only). Last reads the Chronicle as intellectual history as well as a source of facts, and argues its first edition was completed in the mid-seventeenth century from materials developed in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

kano-chronicle-gijimasu.title: Gijimasu (with the Kano Chronicle passage on the first wall)
kano-chronicle-gijimasu.author: Wikipedia contributors, quoting Palmer's 1908 translation of the Kano Chronicle
kano-chronicle-gijimasu.kind: primary source passage reproduced in an encyclopedia article
kano-chronicle-gijimasu.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Reign 1095-1134 by the Chronicle's reckoning. "They began the wall from Raria", on to the gate of Bazugar, the water gate and the gate of Adama.

kano-chronicle-yusa.title: Yusa (Tsaraki) (with the Kano Chronicle passage on the walls)
kano-chronicle-yusa.author: Wikipedia contributors, quoting Palmer's 1908 translation of the Kano Chronicle
kano-chronicle-yusa.kind: primary source passage reproduced in an encyclopedia article
kano-chronicle-yusa.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Reign 1136-1194 by the Chronicle's reckoning; the Chronicle says he completed the walls of Kano. The UNESCO tentative-list file instead credits Zamnagawa in the mid-14th century.

kano-chronicle-rumfa.title: Muhammad Rumfa (with the Kano Chronicle passage on his reign, Palmer 1908)
kano-chronicle-rumfa.author: Wikipedia contributors, quoting Palmer's 1908 translation of the Kano Chronicle
kano-chronicle-rumfa.kind: primary source passage reproduced in an encyclopedia article
kano-chronicle-rumfa.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. In order: he built the Dakin Rimfa; the next year he entered his house; the next year he extended the walls from Kofan Dagachi towards Kofan Mata, on to Kofan Gertawasa and Kofan Kawayi, and from Kofan Naissa to Kofan Kansakali; he established the Kurmi market. First war with Katsina, 11 years, neither side winning. Ruled 37 years (1463-1499 by later reckoning). The Chronicle itself gives no calendar years and does not name al-Maghili.

unesco-kano-walls.title: Ancient Kano City Walls and Associated Sites (Tentative List)
unesco-kano-walls.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre; submitted by Nigeria's National Commission for Museums and Monuments, 8 Oct 2007
unesco-kano-walls.kind: heritage nomination file (the state party's own description, not yet evaluated)
unesco-kano-walls.rights: Facts cited; no text or images reproduced.
unesco-kano-walls.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Dala hill: settlement site "dating back to the 10th century AD". Wall foundation laid by Gijimasu 1095-1134; completed in the middle of the 14th century under Zamnagawa; extended to its present position in the 16th century. Gates as old as the walls. Kurmi among the oldest markets. Palace built by Muhammadu Rumfa (1463-1499).

wiki-dalla-hill.title: Dalla Hill
wiki-dalla-hill.author: Wikipedia contributors (citing Iliffe, Africans: The History of a Continent, 2007, and the Kano Chronicle)
wiki-dalla-hill.kind: encyclopedia article citing a scholarly survey; secondary
wiki-dalla-hill.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. An iron-working community on the hill from about the seventh century (Iliffe). The Kano Chronicle remembers Barbushe as keeper of the Tsumburbura shrine on Dala: oral tradition, undated.

archnet-gidan-rumfa.title: Gidan Rumfa
archnet-gidan-rumfa.author: ArchNet (Aga Khan Trust for Culture and MIT Libraries), with bibliography (Dmochowski 1990, Saad 1981)
archnet-gidan-rumfa.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Built in the fifteenth century by Sarkin Rumfa, about 1480; its grounds occupy the highest space in Kano. Many gates were originally circular entrance vestibules and became rectangular in an early twentieth-century change; the bold painted designs probably date from the 1930s and 1940s. Gates set up a hierarchy of space through a series of courtyards (processional access).

wiki-kurmi-market.title: Kurmi Market
wiki-kurmi-market.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-kurmi-market.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Founded under Muhammad Rumfa in the fifteenth century and still trading in Kano's old city. Its later slave market is not part of this scene.

verskin-maghili.title: al-Maghili
verskin-maghili.author: Alan Verskin, Encyclopaedia of Islam, Third Edition (2019), author's copy
verskin-maghili.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Muhammad al-Maghili wrote Taj al-din, advice on the duties of kings, for Muhammad Rumfa of Kano (translated by Bedri and Starratt, Kano Studies, 1974).

osiboye-2016-kano-walls.title: A Survey of Styles and Functions of Kano Ancient City Wall and Gates
osiboye-2016-kano-walls.author: O. O. Osiboye, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria
osiboye-2016-kano-walls.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026 (record page). The survey still identifies Kofar Kansakali and Kofar Na'isa among Kano's gates. Gate positions for the fifteenth century are not established here; the setting places gates schematically.

africanlegacy-kano-walls.title: Kano city walls
africanlegacy-kano-walls.author: African Legacy project, Bournemouth University
africanlegacy-kano-walls.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. The walls are built of sun-dried earth blocks called tubali, described as pear-shaped.

wiki-hausa-architecture.title: Hausa architecture
wiki-hausa-architecture.author: Wikipedia contributors (after John Moughtin, Hausa Architecture, 1985)
wiki-hausa-architecture.kind: encyclopedia article summarising an architectural study; secondary
wiki-hausa-architecture.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Laterite earth as the main building material; walls of tubali; city walls with a sloping profile, crenellated crest and loopholes.
